set.body:
Current release queue, 7 October 2026: release-1.0; milestone-video.
Plan: docs/refactor/RELEASE-QUEUE.md. Mote remains authoritative; one primary agent and at most one helper.

Reconciliation: FrameSet stream identity and scene-frame planning fixes are landed. Existing planning receipts do not prove seek/media correspondence, caption correctness, or full raw-video command completion.

Remaining / next action: Finish checked caption request/extent, multipart loader and executed ordinal-frame correspondence; then expose raw video -> timed shot/caption source and its annotation-sidecar join through the public command.

Release tags schedule work; they do not establish completion or empirical qualification. Use current AGENTS.md for ownership, scoped gates and exact-SHA review; old fleet roles, timers and fixed gate task counts are historical. Keep the original scientific preregistration, denominators, admission and sealed-test rules below.

Retained acceptance and design context:

Owner MVP: ingest videos alone and video/recall pairs without hand annotations, and supply the video half of video+annotations. Today the media module has ffprobe packet-index ingest and frame/caption contracts (media/src/main/scala/storymodel4s/media/frames.scala, caption.scala) plus Python workers (media/worker/scenedetect_worker.py, media/worker-vlm/caption_worker.py), but no command and no producer of the captions JSON the mapper reads. The bench caption loader does not replay media receipt checks, and tools/recall-study/extract_scene_frames.py:148-152 keeps only the majority part of a scene that crosses a part boundary (docs/design/sherlock-fmri-analysis-readiness-2026-09-22.md, integration gaps).

Acceptance:
1. One documented command takes raw video file(s) (one or more parts of one edition) and writes a checked timed source package in the same source contract the mapping facade consumes (the timed-source contract that bd-01M35B05TC6GBED9Z3HZMX618E migrates out of embed-bench). No hand annotation is required.
2. Stages: ffprobe packet index (media) -> shot/scene boundaries (existing PySceneDetect worker) -> frame sampling with exact per-part extents -> per-segment VLM captions (existing worker) -> segments carrying description, exact playback interval, part/edition identity and caption provenance.
3. Frame extraction is part-correct: a scene crossing parts yields per-part extents, never a majority-part substitution. A straddling-scene fixture fails under the old majority rule and passes under the fix.
4. A caption loader replays the media adapter's model/frame/receipt checks. A mismatched edition, a missing receipt, or a caption for an unsampled frame refuses. The bench sidecar path is rerouted through this loader or documented as legacy.
5. The package serves both as the caption sidecar for the video+annotations arm (joined to an annotation source by edition and time) and as the sole source for video+recall without annotations. Partial coverage is explicit: unsampled spans are gaps, not empty descriptions.
6. Missing local tools or models fail offline with an actionable missing-capability result. There is no automatic download or hosted fallback. The package records model and runtime digests.

Evidence: exact-SHA checkAll with bound totals; named mutations for the part-extent and receipt checks; SD6 cold review. No claim about caption accuracy, or about coverage of dialogue or fleeting action.
